_comment: Single source of truth for the interview guide (spine topics, criteria, caps). Imported by scripts/sim_interview.mjs (harness) and intended for src/components/BackgroundInterview.tsx (live). 'stakeholdersRevised' is the depth-first stakeholders variant, applied when REVISED_STAKEHOLDERS=1.

questions.text: To start, what's your current role and field?
criteria: Named their job title or role. Any brief mention is sufficient.
It is clear what field or industry they work in.

questions.text: And how long have you been in this role?
criteria: Indicated roughly how long they've been in this role — a rough range is enough (e.g. 'a few years', 'just started'), and a tenure cue already given earlier ('first-year PhD', 'new grad') also satisfies this. Do NOT re-ask or clarify duration once any answer is present; accept it and move on.

questions.text: What are your primary responsibilities at work?
criteria: FLOOR (basically single-touch) — once they've named what they're responsible for, or even just what they do, this topic is COVERED. Granular activities count — the typical-week question right after captures the task-level detail, so do NOT re-probe here to 'lift the altitude'. NEVER re-ask the responsibilities question in reworded form ('What are your main responsibilities?' then 'What would you say you're mainly responsible for?' is the repeat to avoid).

ONLY follow up if the answer was genuinely EMPTY or evasive ('a bit of everything', 'hard to say', 'depends'). When you do, make it a GENUINELY different question — don't restate the topic; nudge for one concrete thing they handle ('What's the main thing that lands on your plate?'). Do NOT use insider phrasing ('areas you own', 'ownership altitude') — that's a note for you, not words to say.

questions.text: Walk me through a typical week. What are the recurring tasks you do?
criteria: FLOOR — named at least one real recurring activity/task. If none, follow up asking what they regularly do.
BREADTH — if only ONE activity, acknowledge then ask whether there are others. If several distinct, covered.

SUBSTANCE — give the TASKS the work involves, not generic labels. If a central activity is a bare label, ask what they have to DO for it (the smaller tasks it breaks into) — NOT its topic. Probe ONE thread per turn.

DEEPEN THE CENTER (lightly) — if ONE activity DOMINATES (e.g. a developer who mostly programs), ask ONCE about the different KINDS of work within that core activity (e.g. 'what are the different kinds of programming work that come up?'). KINDS of work = tasks, not content. ONE such follow-up is enough — do NOT exhaustively decompose the core across several turns. Covered as soon as the core has more than a bare label, or if no single activity dominates.
RESPONSIBILITY COVERAGE — if a responsibility named earlier does NOT map to a task they mentioned, follow up ONCE asking whether they regularly do anything on it. Probe ONE per turn.

questions.text: What do you produce or deliver in your work?
criteria: FLOOR — named at least one concrete output/artifact. If NONE, follow up asking what they produce/maintain/deliver.

DELIVERY & UPKEEP (not building) — focus on FINISHING/DELIVERY: what they do to get it READY and OUT or keep it up to date (checking, formatting, approval, sending, maintenance). Do NOT re-ask how they build it. If clear or would just repeat building, covered.
BREADTH — if only ONE output, ask whether there are others. If several, covered.

questions.text: Who do you do your work for or with — the people, teams, or clients you deal with?
questions.closingQuestion: Last one: if someone shadowed you for two weeks, what tasks would they see that we haven't named yet?
criteria: FLOOR — named at least one person/team/role/outside party they work for or with. If NONE, follow up asking who they work for or with.

RELATIONAL TASKS (PRIORITIZE) — the goal is the COMMUNICATION/INTERPERSONAL tasks each relationship carries, but ask about it as INTERACTION / ENGAGEMENT, not as another 'what work do you do' question: 'How do you usually interact with them?', 'How do you engage with them day to day?', 'What do those interactions usually look like?'. Avoid the flat 'what do you do with them / what work do you do together' framing. Aim to surface relational tasks, do NOT lead. Probe ONE relationship per turn.
BREADTH (secondary) — only if ONE party and others clearly exist; do NOT reflexively ask 'who else'.
FLOOR — named at least one person/team/role/outside party they work for or with. If NONE, follow up asking who they work for or with.

RELATIONAL TASKS (THE GOAL) — surface the concrete COMMUNICATION / COORDINATION tasks of the SINGLE most central relationship they named — what they run, write, report, hand off, review, escalate, present, or give/get feedback on (e.g. running the weekly sync, writing the client update, reporting to a manager). When that party is a bare label, follow up ONCE with a clear, plain, OPEN question framed as INTERACTION / ENGAGEMENT — 'How do you usually interact with them?', 'How do you engage with them?', 'What do those interactions usually look like?' — rather than the flat 'what do you do with/for them'. Aim to surface the relational tasks, do NOT lead. ONE follow-up is enough; do NOT work through every party.

GO DEEPER, NOT WIDER — do NOT ask 'who else do you work with'. The goal is the communication tasks, not collecting names. Covered once the single most central relationship carries one concrete task — then move on; do NOT keep drilling additional relationships.
